# Accordion

Accordion organizes related sections that can be expanded in place without navigating away from the current page.

## Import

```tsx
import { Accordion } from '@vellira-ui/react';
```

## When To Use

- Progressive disclosure in settings, FAQs, summaries, and dense detail pages.
- Use single mode when one section should stay in focus at a time.
- Use multiple mode when users need to compare details across sections.
- Use Tabs instead when sections are peer views that should occupy the same level of navigation.

## Accessibility

- Accordion.Trigger renders a native button and exposes expanded state with aria-expanded.
- Each trigger is connected to its content region with aria-controls.
- Native button keyboard behavior supports Tab navigation plus Enter and Space activation.
- Disabled accordions or items are removed from interaction through disabled button semantics.

## See Also

- [Tabs](/react/tabs) - Tabs for peer sections that act like page-level views.
- [Dropdown](/react/dropdown) - Dropdown for compact menus and action lists.
- [Popover](/react/popover) - Popover for floating contextual content.

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { Accordion } from '@vellira-ui/react';

<Accordion defaultValue='billing'>
  <Accordion.Item value='billing'>
    <Accordion.Trigger>Billing</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>
      View invoices, update payment methods, and manage plan limits.
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>

  <Accordion.Item value='security'>
    <Accordion.Trigger>Security</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>
      Review passkeys, sessions, and recovery options.
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>;
```

## Parts

| Part                | Purpose                                         |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `Accordion`         | Root state, selection mode, and disabled state. |
| `Accordion.Item`    | Value-scoped section container.                 |
| `Accordion.Trigger` | Button that opens or closes an item.            |
| `Accordion.Content` | Panel rendered for the matching item.           |

Accordion is value-based. Use stable string values so items can be reordered,
inserted, or conditionally rendered without changing the expanded state.

## Single And Multiple Mode

Single mode is the default and keeps one item open at a time:

```tsx
<Accordion defaultValue='profile'>...</Accordion>
```

Multiple mode accepts arrays for `value` and `defaultValue`:

```tsx
<Accordion type='multiple' defaultValue={['profile', 'billing']}>
  ...
</Accordion>
```

## Controlled State

Use controlled state when the expanded item should sync with routing,
persistence, analytics, or another part of the page.

```tsx
const [section, setSection] = useState('profile');

<Accordion value={section} onValueChange={setSection}>
  ...
</Accordion>;
```

For multiple mode, control state with a `string[]`.

## Collapsible Sections

In single mode, the open item stays open by default when activated again. Add
`collapsible` when the current item may close and leave the accordion with no
expanded section:

```tsx
<Accordion collapsible defaultValue='notifications'>
  ...
</Accordion>
```

`collapsible` is not used in multiple mode because each open item can already be
closed independently.

## Disabled State

Disable every item at the root:

```tsx
<Accordion disabled>...</Accordion>
```

Disable one section on `Accordion.Item` when only that section is unavailable:

```tsx
<Accordion.Item value='enterprise' disabled>
  ...
</Accordion.Item>
```

## Mounting

Collapsed content is unmounted by default. Use `forceMount` when a panel must
stay mounted for measurement, animation coordination, or preserving local state:

```tsx
<Accordion.Content forceMount>
  <PersistentEditor />
</Accordion.Content>
```

## Keyboard And Accessibility

`Accordion.Trigger` renders a native `button`, so browser keyboard behavior is
preserved. Users can move through triggers with `Tab` and activate a trigger
with `Enter` or `Space`.

Each trigger exposes `aria-expanded` and is connected to its content with
`aria-controls`. Keep trigger labels short and distinct, and avoid placing
unrelated interactive controls inside a trigger label.
